brief: Different caller personalities physically form some letters in the NextCaller wordmark.

concepts.title: E — The Line-up
concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Create a fresh illustrated wordmark concept for NextCaller, a playful creative studio for human-hosted phone-in shows with fictional callers. The user's specific creative direction is: different caller personalities MUST physically form some of the letters. This is character-driven typography.
The exact word is "nextcaller", spelled n e x t c a l l e r, all ten letters exactly once, clearly legible in that order, lowercase, on one horizontal baseline.
The people are built into and help form the letter silhouettes: their bodies, posture, arms, head and negative spaces are the letter strokes themselves. Do NOT place a row of faces above, below or next to an otherwise ordinary wordmark. Do NOT merely stick googly eyes on normal letters. Person and letter should be one ingenious drawing.
Only three or four letters become callers; retain quiet, beautifully drawn bold lettering for the others so the name reads instantly. Depict a varied fictional adult cast with distinct body types, hairstyles and moods, such as an indignant ranter, a warm chatty gossip and a deadpan dry comic. Witty and full of personality, never corporate or infantile. Restrict the facial detail to a few expressive shapes. The main outlines should remain comprehensible at small website-header size.
One finished concept only, centered horizontal wordmark with generous clear margins on pure white. No separate logo symbol, no tagline or other text, no grid or mockup. Crisp flat vector-like illustration, no gradients, texture, glow, 3D, stock microphone, Wi-Fi symbol, sparkle, or generic telephone emblem.
Direction: editorial cartoon meets confidently chunky contemporary sans-serif. Keep "nextc" and "er" navy #062551. Transform the central "a", "l", "l" into three unmistakable adult personalities: a round animated gossip whose curved body and bent arm form the a's bowl and counter; a tall rigid disgruntled caller forming the first l, with a squared bent foot as its lower terminal; a slightly leaning relaxed dry comic forming the second l. Let the characters subtly interact and look toward each other without breaking the letter spacing. Cyan #38d3ee and warm yellow #f5d95d give the three characters distinct clothing accents. The result should read "nextcaller" immediately, with the human shapes revealed on a second look.
